audit_scope: Bounded local reconciliation/catalog/interface-census/finding-lifecycle paths plus pinned inventory of 26 visible non-archived repositories, two search rounds, and recursive Git-tree inventories for all 13 repositories without code-search indexing.

consumers_and_producers.rule: DETECTED records discovery output only; it does not establish complete catalog coverage or VERIFIED status.
Schema validity and candidate-record validation do not promote candidates to CONFIRMED or VERIFIED.
Preserve the legacy report's own status and parser-coverage limitations. Do not promote its DETECTED output based on zero deltas or the independent report.
RECONCILED is scoped to the two supplied inventories and expected-delta contract; the producer explicitly states it is not VERIFIED.
The ledger requires independent RECONCILED plus zero blockers for its own resolution logic; RESOLVED does not imply merge approval or organization-wide VERIFIED status.
RECONCILED and VERIFIED counts are distinct. RECONCILED claims require reconciled contracts; VERIFIED claims require every contract to be VERIFIED. The current census is required to remain BLOCKED.
Unknown counts remain null and must not be treated as zero; the report preserves its explicit limitations.
Schema acceptance validates shape only; it is not proof of source completeness or verification.
VERIFIED requires exact-SHA checks and Run/Job/Step evidence; keep this lifecycle separate from legacy report statuses.
These values describe a finding's remediation lifecycle, not the status of reconciliation-report.json or the independent reconciliation gate. No implicit cross-domain mapping is allowed.
The lifecycle is separate from report status semantics.
Tests verify only the validator's defined reconciliation scope.
Negative tests reject implicit promotions, missing/invalid evidence, unknown statuses, incomplete organization scope, and commit-head mismatch.

residuals: Repository listing and main-branch SHA pinning are complete for all 26 non-archived repositories visible to the authenticated account; seven archived repositories remain outside active scope unless governance includes them.

Thirteen of the 26 active repositories are not indexed for code search. Their recursive Git trees were enumerated at pinned SHAs (all non-truncated), but candidate file contents are not all directly inspected.

Direct inspection of representative candidates found domain-separated catalog statuses, draft specs, local audit tools, governance workflows, and a VM execution-receipt gate. No inspected excerpt established a new consumer of the PR #29 reconciliation-report status contract, but absence of a consumer has not been proven.
The other 13 code-search-indexed repositories still require content-level source inspection at pinned SHAs; code-search results alone are insufficient to classify all readers/writers.
Complete exact-ref inspection and classification of all candidate workflows, scripts, schemas, report producers, status readers/writers, and generated consumers remains incomplete.
Consumer-specific negative regressions for every executable PR #29 status consumer and per-repository exact-SHA workflow/job/step/artifact evidence binding remain incomplete.
Audit closure remains blocked; status must stay PARTIAL / BLOCKED / NOT VERIFIED.
repository_inventory: Main SHAs pinned for all 26 visible non-archived repositories. Recursive Git Trees API returned non-truncated trees for all 13 not indexed for code search; this is path inventory, not content-level audit.
